core_obligations: Degree zero (proof lines 1934-1944): the statement for p = 0 is true because the product of sheaves has as sections the product of the sections, and the section functor commutes with products.

Degree one (proof lines 1944-1959): for p = 1 the author compares the two sides through an injective resolution and shows that the canonical map is injective, using the exactness properties of products of abelian groups and the description of the first cohomology as a quotient of the kernel of the first differential.
proof_roadmap: Compute the degree zero case directly from sections.
For degree one, compare both sides through an injective resolution of the product.
Use the exactness properties of products of abelian groups to see that the comparison map is injective.
difficulty_reason: The lemma compares the cohomology of a product of abelian sheaves with the product of their cohomologies, showing the canonical map is an isomorphism in degree zero and injective in degree one (statement lines 1921-1932). The degree-zero case is immediate from the description of sections of a product (proof lines 1934-1944). The degree-one case requires a comparison through an injective resolution of the product and uses the exactness properties of products of abelian groups to obtain injectivity (proof lines 1944-1959). The non-formal content is the degree-one comparison. The claim is H2: one immediate case and one comparison of complexes.
